news.raw_snippet: We wrap up our coverage of the markets and the week. In this week’s newsletter:. On the surface, it was a quiet week for stocks, but there was plenty going on throughout the markets. It’s not just established hardware stocks, like SanDisk, up more than 400% this year alone: the party is roaring among IPOs. The main event was the red-hot Cerebras IPO which came close to tripling on its first day of trading. We took a close look at Cerebras and how it appears to have hit a sweet spot in the AI infrastructure buildout. This past week also furthered the trend of how non-tech stocks are being swept up in the AI buildout frenzy. That’s even the case for renewable energy, as seen in the IPO of Fervo, a geothermal energy company that has a business plan that involves piping energy directly to data centers and whose stock jumped 35% in its debut.

news.snippet: 此趋势引发对就业市场结构性变化的深度担忧，Entry-level岗位面临被替代风险。
news.raw_snippet: ### Download App. NewsJobsNearly half of CEOs don't want to hire entry-level employees as AI can do their work: Study. # Nearly half of CEOs don't want to hire entry-level employees as AI can do their work: Study. ## A global survey found that nearly half of CEOs across the world plan to reduce entry-level hiring as AI is increasingly taking over routine workplace tasks and reshaping how companies build their workforce. Nearly half of CEOs across the world do not want to hire for entry-level jobs anymore. According to a new global survey by the Oliver Wyman Forum and the New York Stock Exchange, companies are planning to move away from hiring freshers and instead focus more on experienced employees, as artificial intelligence is already helping take care of many routine entry-level tasks. The 2026 CEO Survey, based on responses from 415 chief executives across industries and regions, found that 43 per cent of CEOs expect to shift away from junior-level roles over the next two years.

news.raw_snippet: Members of the editorial and news staff of the USA TODAY Network were not involved in the creation of this content.*** |. *As AI adoption accelerates, Proven ROI launches AI Governance services to help businesses create standards and reduce risk.*. It should create the foundation that allows organizations to scale AI with confidence.”**. John Cronin, CEO and founder of Proven ROI, believes businesses have focused heavily on the speed and advantages of AI adoption while spending far less time establishing standards for how AI should be managed, monitored, and governed over time. According to Cronin, many organizations now have employees independently experimenting with AI tools, teams deploying automation solutions, and departments implementing AI powered systems without company wide standards around oversight, accountability, or operational guidelines. “Businesses rushed to adopt AI because of the opportunities it creates,” said John Cronin, CEO of Proven ROI. AI Governance refers to the policies, frameworks, standards, and oversight structures organizations use to guide how artificial intelligence technologies are implemented and managed.
